content: Fosaprepitant is indicated for use in adults and children aged 6 months and older to prevent both acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC), including high-dose cisplatin, as well as moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (MEC). Chronic continuous administration of fosaprepitant is not recommended due to a lack of studies and the potential for changes in its drug interaction profile over time. The following drug interactions with fosaprepitant are clinically significant: 1. Chloramphenicol, Danazol, and Darunavir: These drugs increase fosaprepitant levels by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Co-administration is contraindicated. 2. Flibanserin: Fosaprepitant increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, which can lead to severe hypotension or syncope. Co-administration is contraindicated. 3. Lomitapide and Lonafarnib: Fosaprepitant significantly increases their levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Pimozide: Fosaprepitant increases pimozide levels, raising the risk of QT interval prolongation. Co-administration is contraindicated. 5. Ribociclib and Tipranavir: These drugs increase fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Apalutamide: This drug decreases fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Avapritinib, Axitinib, and Bosutinib: Fosaprepitant increases their levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Carbamazepine and Ceritinib: These drugs alter fosaprepitant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Cimetidine and Clarithromycin: These drugs increase fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Cobicistat: Fosaprepitant increases cobicistat levels, and vice versa, through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Everolimus: Fosaprepitant increases everolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Fentanyl (all formulations): Fosaprepitant increases fentanyl levels, raising the risk of respiratory depression and sedation. Monitor closely and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 13. Ibrutinib: Fosaprepitant increases ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or interrupt ibrutinib therapy if short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary. 14. Itraconazole and Ketoconazole: These drugs increase fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Lovastatin and Simvastatin: Fosaprepitant increases their levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Midazolam (intranasal): Fosaprepitant increases midazolam levels, potentially prolonging sedation. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Mifepristone: This drug increases fosaprepitant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Neratinib and Venetoclax: Fosaprepitant increases their levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the dose of these drugs as per prescribing information. 19. Olaparib: Fosaprepitant increases olaparib levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. 20. Pazopanib and Pemigatinib: Fosaprepitant increases their levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the dose of these drugs as per prescribing information. 21. Ranolazine: Fosaprepitant increases ranolazine levels, raising the risk of QT interval prolongation. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Rifampin and St. John’s Wort: These drugs decrease fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Siponimod: Fosaprepitant increases siponimod levels. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors plus CYP2C9 inhibitors is not recommended. 24. Tolvaptan: Fosaprepitant increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Venetoclax: Fosaprepitant increases venetoclax levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicities. 26. Vilazodone: Fosaprepitant increases vilazodone levels. If intolerable adverse effects occur, reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 27. Amiodarone, Alprazolam, and Amitriptyline: Fosaprepitant increases their levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Armodafinil: This drug decreases fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Atorvastatin: Fosaprepitant increases atorvastatin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Budesonide: Fosaprepitant increases budesonide levels, and vice versa, through CYP3A4 interactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Buprenorphine (all formulations): Fosaprepitant increases buprenorphine levels. Monitor for signs of overmedication or withdrawal and adjust therapy as needed. 32. Buspirone: Fosaprepitant increases buspirone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Cabazitaxel: Fosaprepitant increases cabazitaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Bortezomib: Fosaprepitant increases bortezomib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Belzutifan: This drug decreases fosaprepitant levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of fosaprepitant. 36. Brexpiprazole: Fosaprepitant increases brexpiprazole levels. Administer one-quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. 37. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Fosaprepitant increases their levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Fosaprepitant increases their levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Avanafil: Fosaprepitant increases avanafil levels. Limit the maximum dose of avanafil to 50 mg once every 24 hours when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Bexarotene: Fosaprepitant increases bexarotene levels. Monitor for altered serum concentrations and adjust therapy as needed. This list highlights the importance of careful monitoring and dose adjustments when fosaprepitant is co-administered with other medications, particularly those metabolized by the CYP3A4 enzyme.
